app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

args.diagnosis: Transient resident memory spike in product-catalog exceeded the Go runtime GOMEMLIMIT, causing the OpenTelemetry exporter to block/timeout/receive "data refused due to high memory usage", which in turn caused gRPC handlers to return 13 INTERNAL errors.
args.reasoning:
1) product-catalog pod logs show exporter failures at 2026/10/19 15:05:17, 15:05:27 and 15:05:31 including: "exporter export timeout: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded" and "traces export: exporter export timeout: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = data refused due to high memory usage" (get_logs call).  
2) Prometheus metrics for the pod in the 60‑minute window show container_memory_usage_bytes peaking ~17,022,976 bytes (and working_set ~15–17MB) while the pod has GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB (in pod env) and a container memory limit of 32Mi (get_metrics_range + kubectl_describe). The memory samples therefore exceed the GOMEMLIMIT around the same timeframe as the exporter timeouts.  
3) Tracing data contains 20 error traces for product-catalog with error_message "13 INTERNAL: Error: Product Catalog Fail" across the same period, indicating client-visible gRPC INTERNAL errors correlated with the exporter timeouts (get_traces).  
4) The pod was not OOMKilled or restarted (restart count 0 and describe events), so this is a transient in-process memory pressure rather than a container eviction (kubectl_describe).  
5) Collector logs show separate OpenSearch exporter mapping errors later (rejections around 15:14–15:14:48), but those are different failures; the product-catalog logs explicitly report data refused due to high memory usage at 15:05:31, which aligns with the pod memory exceeding GOMEMLIMIT and the timing of the 13 INTERNAL traces (get_logs of otel-collector and pod logs).  
Conclusion: transient in-process memory pressure in product-catalog (memory briefly exceeded the app's GOMEMLIMIT) caused the telemetry exporter to block/timeout/refuse data, which cascaded into the application returning gRPC 13 INTERNAL errors. Recommended next steps (not executed here): increase GOMEMLIMIT or fix memory spike, enable exporter sending_queue/retries, and investigate code path causing memory growth.

message_history.content: Final diagnosis submitted successfully. Investigation complete.

final_report.root_cause: A transient in-process memory spike in the product-catalog process caused the Go runtime to exceed its GOMEMLIMIT (16MiB). While the container memory limit (32MiB) remained available and the pod was not OOMKilled, the Go allocator hit its in-process limit which caused the OpenTelemetry exporter to block/timeout and return "data refused due to high memory usage". The exporter blocking/unavailable state cascaded into the application's gRPC handlers returning client-visible 13 INTERNAL errors, causing customer requests to fail.
affected_resources: pod/otel-collector (observed telemetry pipeline errors later; separate mapping rejections)
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) product-catalog logs at 2026-10-19T15:05:17–15:05:31 contain repeated exporter failures: "exporter export timeout: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded" and "traces export: exporter export timeout: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = data refused due to high memory usage." 2) Prometheus metrics (60m window) show container_memory_usage_bytes and working_set peaking ~15–17 MiB (one sample ~17,022,976 bytes) while the pod has GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB set; container_spec_memory_limit_bytes = 32MiB. Observed memory samples thus exceed the GOMEMLIMIT at the same timeframe as exporter errors. 3) Tracing shows ~20 error traces during the same window with error_message "13 INTERNAL: Error: Product Catalog Fail", proving client-visible failures correlated with exporter errors. 4) The pod was not OOMKilled nor restarted (restart count 0), indicating an in-process memory pressure event rather than container eviction. 5) Additional signals: a spike in network tx/rx around the failure and a previous container_threads_max sample (11557) indicate transient resource spikes; otel-collector logs show separate mapping/rejection errors later (~15:14) but those are temporally distinct and not the proximate cause of the 15:05 product-catalog failures.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority 1 (platform/resource exhaustion) and Priority 2 (DB connectivity) investigations were completed. For priority 1 we correlated pod logs, Prometheus metrics, and traces: logs show exporter timeouts and memory-refused messages; metrics show memory exceeding GOMEMLIMIT at the same times; traces show gRPC 13 INTERNAL errors for product-catalog in that window. kubectl describe showed GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB and container memory limit 32MiB, with no restarts/OOM events. For priority 2 we validated DB connectivity/config — the product-catalog DB_CONNECTION_STRING, postgresql-init ConfigMap, astronomy-db Service and pod readiness all match and show no authentication/connectivity errors, ruling out DB issues. From the correlated evidence we conclude the causal chain: transient resident memory spike -> Go runtime hit GOMEMLIMIT -> OpenTelemetry exporter blocked/refused data -> application gRPC handlers returned 13 INTERNAL errors. Recommended remediations (not executed here) include increasing GOMEMLIMIT or fixing the allocation spike, enabling exporter sending_queue and retries, adding exporter timeouts/fail-open behavior, and instrumenting the pod to capture process-level memory and heap profiles at the time of spikes to find the offending code path.
